title: Compact Defaults Generator and 'compactize' cost-impact CLI
author: Priya Gupta
description: Motivation: Customers frequently ask for a small-surface, conservative defaults pack that reduces per-token costs for bursty web workloads while preserving latency SLOs. This PR introduces a Compact Defaults Generator and a small CLI (compactize) that produces tenant-scoped batch/caching/quant presets plus a dry-run cost-impact estimator. Summary: 1) a generator that converts profiling samples into conservative defaults (batch shapes, prefix/KV cache window, safe quant profiles), 2) a compactize CLI to preview cost and latency delta in dry-run mode, 3) runtime adapters to accept compact defaults as a named preset, 4) docs and e2e smoke-tests. Checklist: - [x] Generator algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] CLI with dry-run and apply modes - [x] Telemetry hooks added for compact preset usage metrics - [x] Docs: compact-defaults.md and quickstart - [x] Backwards-compatible: generator emits presets that the runtime treats as non-breaking - [x] Performance/latency smoke tests included How it works: The generator ingests a small sample of request traces (shape histogram + prefix-hit rates) and applies a conservative shrink-wrapping heuristic: prefer lower batch_size ceilings for latency-sensitive routes, set KV cache retention to min(window, 2*median-seq) and attach a quant-profile tag limited to known-safe FP16/INT8 candidates. The CLI runs a lightweight simulator (token-cost and token-latency model derived from recent telemetry) to estimate per-tenant token USD delta and P50/P95 latency delta. Usage: compactize dry-run --profile sample.json --tenant tenant-42 returns a JSON table of estimated 30d cost delta and percentile latency delta. compactize apply --preset-name compact-lite --tenant tenant-42 writes the preset to tenant defaults API (requires admin scope). Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag compact_defaults.v1, start with opt-in for internal tenants, run 2-week analysis before wide enablement. Backwards compatibility and safety: presets are additive and annotated with rollback metadata and conservative guardbands; runtime will never auto-upgrade an active preset without explicit rollout policy. Related: builds on earlier telemetry and prefilling work (see ENG-900/ENG-1423).

review_comments: Marco Alvarez (reviewer): Generator looks good overall; please add a short unit test that covers a skewed sequence length distribution where median<<90th so we exercise the KV retention clamp.
Priya Gupta (author reply): Added test 'test_kv_retention_clamp' and updated the algorithm comment to explain the clamp rationale.

Chen Li (reviewer): CLI dry-run output is useful but needs clearer labeling for cost sign (savings vs increase). Also, please make the simulator deterministic by seeding the RNG when --seed is not provided.
Priya Gupta (author reply): Fixed labels in dry-run table, exposed --seed default (42) for deterministic simulation. Added an explanatory note in the CLI help output.
Ayesha Khan (reviewer): Telemetry event cardinality looks safe; please confirm the event tag values (preset_name, tenant_class) are capped to known enums to avoid high-cardinality tags.
Priya Gupta (author reply): Telemetry now emits preset_name limited to the first 64 chars and tenant_class derived from our existing tenant_tiers enum; updated the event schema file.

release_notes: Added Compact Defaults Generator and 'compactize' CLI: a conservative preset generator and cost/latency dry-run tool to produce tenant-scoped batching/caching/quant defaults. Initial rollout behind feature flag compact_defaults.v1. CLI supports dry-run reporting and apply mode to tenant defaults API.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind flag compact_defaults.v1; ops should monitor compact.preset.apply and compact.estimate telemetry events for unexpected cost regressions. Default guardbands added to prevent automatic elevation of batch ceilings.
